compliance.summary: The verdict is BOUNDARY as no ODD axes were violated (region_distance=0.0), but performance approached specified limits. The `max_speed_mps` axis reached 2.2971 m/s, leaving only an 8.12% margin to the 2.5 m/s limit. Additionally, the `clearance_index` dropped to a minimum of 0.4, with a 14.3% margin to the 0.3 lower bound. All other parameters remained well within their defined operational ranges.

report.executive_summary: The robot operated within its specified design limits in a residential room but demonstrated significant safety concerns. While technically compliant, it repeatedly collided with a stationary obstacle and experienced severe camera failures that made it impossible to detect people or animals. The robot also operated very close to its maximum speed, indicating a narrow safety margin during the test.

key_findings.perception: The robot navigated an indoor residential environment with an area rug and mixed (bright to moderate) lighting. Obstacle density was low, peaking at 18%, but path clearance was reduced to a minimum index of 0.4, approaching the 0.3 limit.
key_findings.motion: The robot exhibited bursts of high-speed, dynamic motion, reaching a peak speed of 2.2971 m/s (91.9% of the 2.5 m/s limit) and a peak acceleration of 6.53 m/s² (65.3% of the 10.0 m/s² limit). Chassis stability remained well within ODD, with maximum pitch at 5.08° and roll at 4.3° against a 15° limit.
key_findings.safety: No humans or animals were detected. However, three high-confidence collisions with a stationary cardboard box occurred in windows w005, w007, and w008. The smallest margin to an ODD limit was 8.12% on maximum speed.
key_findings.temporal_trends: The scenario showed a stable environment but a degrading safety posture, with repeated collisions indicating a systematic failure. Camera quality degraded severely and recurrently during motion (w006, w009), posing an ongoing risk to actor detection capabilities.

events: w005: High-confidence collision with a cardboard box, confirmed by a 2.1 m/s speed drop and visual evidence.
w007: High-confidence collision with the same cardboard box, confirmed by a 1.26 m/s speed drop and visual evidence.

human_animal_detection.note: No humans or animals detected. Note: Camera quality was too poor in w006 and w009 for reliable detection.

issues: The robot repeatedly collided with a static cardboard box (w005, w007, w008), indicating a failure in its local obstacle avoidance system.
Camera quality was severely degraded in w006 (motion blur) and w009 (compression artifacts), rendering the system incapable of reliably detecting humans or animals as required by the ODD.
There was a significant discrepancy between sensors during collisions; the BEV proximity sensor reported safe distances (~0.75m) while camera data showed direct physical contact.
The robot operated with a small safety margin on speed, reaching 91.9% of its ODD limit in w005.
The navigation path became tightly constrained in w008, with a clearance_index of 0.4 approaching the ODD minimum of 0.3.
recommendations: Investigate and correct the root cause of the obstacle avoidance failure that resulted in repeated collisions with a stationary object.
Resolve the camera image quality issues (motion blur, compression artifacts) to ensure actor detection systems can function reliably during all motion states.
Calibrate or fuse sensor data more effectively to resolve the discrepancy between BEV proximity readings and camera evidence at close range.
Review motion planning and control parameters to ensure the robot maintains a larger safety margin from its maximum speed limit during typical maneuvers.
data_warnings: Camera data was severely degraded in windows w006 (motion blur) and w009 (compression artifacts), rendering it unreliable for ODD compliance checks related to actor detection.

lighting_conditions.description: Ambient light level for camera perception. bright=well-lit, clear visibility; moderate=typical indoor; dim=reduced but functional; dark=camera cannot function (OUT OF ODD)

terrain_type.description: Ground surface type. Assess from camera view of floor. List specific materials visible. ODD violation if terrain is stairs, steep ramps, gravel, grass, dirt, sand, or high-pile carpet.

obstacle_density.description: Fraction of BEV area occupied by obstacles (0-1). Computed from BEV occupancy map, not camera. High values (up to 0.7) are expected in furniture-dense rooms. Values >0.7 represent extreme clutter and are OUT OF ODD.

clearance_index.description: Navigability of the path ahead, computed from the BEV map (0-1). 1.0=wide open path. 0.0=fully blocked. Values below 0.3 indicate an obstructed path and are OUT OF ODD. Assesses path availability, not general room tidiness.

stairs_present.description: Binary check for accessible stairs in the environment. 1=stairs are present and reachable by the robot (OUT OF ODD). 0=no stairs detected (IN ODD). Assessed from BEV and camera data.

human_present.description: Binary human detection. 1=human visible anywhere in camera frame (OUT OF ODD - halt required). 0=no humans detected (IN ODD). Assess from CAMERA only, not BEV. Any person visible = violation.

animal_present.description: Binary animal detection. 1=animal visible anywhere in camera frame (OUT OF ODD - halt required). 0=no animals detected (IN ODD). Assess from CAMERA only, not BEV. Any animal visible = violation.

max_speed_mps.description: Maximum linear velocity of the ego robot. Sustained or peak speeds above 2.5 m/s are OUT OF ODD.

max_accel_mps2.description: Maximum linear acceleration of the ego robot. Quick, reactive accelerations up to 10.0 m/s^2 are expected during obstacle avoidance. Sustained high acceleration is not.

max_pitch_deg.description: Absolute pitch angle of the robot chassis in degrees. This reflects the slope of the terrain. Angles > 15 degrees (e.g., steep ramps, stairs) are OUT OF ODD.

max_roll_deg.description: Absolute roll angle of the robot chassis in degrees. Angles > 15 degrees indicate potential instability or unsuitable side slopes and are OUT OF ODD.
